notes: Direct HTTP fetch throughout, no blocking. Nav items 'New in' and 'New collection'/'Discover the new collection' all resolve to the SAME editorial media article (/en-eu/media/article/collection-interieur-parisien) -- a lookbook/story page with no product grid -- excluded per brief Sec.3 as marketing/editorial, not a PLP. Checked full /api/collections-sitemap.xml handle list (268 unique handles) for new-arrivals-type terms (nouveau, new, arriv, edition) in English and French: found /collections/nouvelles-editions ('New Editions'). This IS a genuine Algolia-backed PLP -- real product grid, breadcrumb JSON-LD, H1='Nouvelles éditions' -- but it is an ORPHAN page: not linked from main nav, header/mega-menu, or footer (only discoverable via the sitemap), and its title/H1 was NOT translated to English even on the en-eu locale (unlike every other checked collection, e.g. 'Most-wanted pieces', 'Our selection of the week'), which is itself a signal the page may be stale/unmaintained. Its product set is genuinely cross-category (cushions, vases, curtains, mirrors, rugs, lighting, candles all present in one 28-item listing), consistent with a 'newest catalogue additions' concept rather than a themed single-capsule 'edition' (contrast with e.g. /collections/edition-leopard, a themed print capsule). qty=28 verified via nbHits=28, nbPages=2, hitsPerPage=24 (ceil(28/24)=2, consistent), exhaustiveNbHits:true, filters scoped exactly to collectionsHandles:"nouvelles-editions". Recorded per brief's 'if genuinely uncertain, still record with flag' instruction rather than dropped. notre-selection-de-la-semaine ('Our selection of the week', nbHits=48) was also inspected -- it is a weekly editorial curation across all categories ('Discover our weekly selection of furniture, decoration, lighting and household linen'), not a recency-based new-arrivals concept -- excluded as curated/editorial, not newest-additions merchandising.
